content.title: COOKING MISTAKES THAT QUIETLY {{DRAIN}} YOUR FOOD'S NUTRIENTS
facts: **Boiling vegetables** – Submerging veggies in water leaches water-soluble vitamins straight into the pot; steam them instead and keep up to twice the nutrients.
**Draining and rinsing beans** – Rinsing canned beans washes away some of the soluble fiber and minerals clinging to the liquid; a quick rinse is fine, a long soak under the tap isn't.
**Overcrowding the pan** – Piling too much in one pan traps steam and makes food stew instead of sear, so you lose that caramelized flavor and end up with soggy, unevenly cooked meals.
**Tossing the cooking water** – Pasta or veggie water often holds minerals and starch that help sauces bind; save a splash instead of pouring it all down the drain.
**Cooking oil at high heat** – Heating delicate oils like extra virgin olive oil past their smoke point breaks them down and creates harsh-tasting compounds; save those for finishing, not frying.
**Salting too early** – Salting watery vegetables like zucchini or eggplant right before cooking pulls out moisture mid-pan, leaving you with limp, steamed-not-roasted results.
**Cutting veggies hours ahead** – Pre-chopping and storing cut produce for too long exposes more surface area to air, speeding up nutrient loss and wilting.

content.caption:
A few of these habits are easier to fix than people think. Take boiling vegetables: once those vitamins seep into the water, they're gone unless you drink the broth, so switching to steaming or a quick sauté keeps far more of the good stuff where it belongs. Overcrowding the pan is another sneaky one — when food is packed too tight, the pan temperature drops and everything releases moisture, which means you're essentially steaming your dinner instead of browning it, losing both flavor and texture. And salting watery vegetables too early draws liquid out through osmosis before the heat even hits, so you end up fighting a soggy pan instead of getting that nice golden edge. Everyone's kitchen setup is different, so adjust as you go.
